summary: Research DaVinci/pro-NLE UX + editor terminology, audit Vance UI jargon, synthesize a redesign plan

layout_plan.change: Replace the two structural anchors that fight DaVinci muscle memory — the buried 2-button Edit/Color toggle in the top header (+page.svelte lines 1431-1448) and the flat 14-tab bottom 'dock' (lines 2128-2170) — with ONE full-width bottom PAGE BAR pinned to the very bottom of the window. Six pages in pipeline order, mirroring DaVinci's Media·Edit·Fusion·Color·Fairlight·Deliver: Media · Edit · Compositor · Color · Audio · Deliver (drop Cut for now). Center the row; each button is icon-on-top + small-caps label; active page gets the amber (vance-accent) fill, the rest dim grey; add a chevron to minimize the bar. This single move converts a developer tab-soup into the layout every Resolve user already navigates by reflex.
layout_plan.why: The page bar IS the DaVinci mental model. Right now a video editor sees 14 undifferentiated tabs and a hidden page toggle and has no idea the app follows the post-production pipeline. Making the pipeline the primary navigation is the highest-familiarity change available.

layout_plan.change: Distribute the 14 dock panels into those pages instead of listing them flat. Deliver = ExportPanel + PublishPanel + ReviewPanel (render settings → queue → review). Audio (Fairlight) = MixerConsole + AiAudioPanel + ControlPanel + MasterMeter as a full-height right-edge channel-strip page. Compositor (Fusion) = FusionPanel. Edit-page tools = MographPanel (Titles), CaptionsPanel, GeneratePanel, ReframePanel, MagneticPanel, HistoryPanel — reachable from the Edit page's left dock / toolbar, not as peer pages. Color page already exists (Nodes + Scopes) and just folds under the Color button.
layout_plan.why: DaVinci groups tools by workflow stage; an editor looks for the mixer under an audio page, not tab #3. Grouping by pipeline stage is what makes the app 'read left-to-right = post-production order.'

layout_plan.change: Move the AiToolsPanel (install/setup of pip/Python/model components) OUT of the page and dock flow entirely into Settings → 'Add-ons'. Render it as DaVinci-plain feature cards: name + size ('AI Image Generation — 4.2 GB') + [Install] + progress bar + 'Ready.' No terminal, no PATH, no Python, no pip badges, no raw log lines.
layout_plan.why: Installing components is setup, not a stage of editing — it should never be a peer of Edit/Color. And it is the single densest source of developer jargon in the app, so relocating + reskinning it kills a whole class of confusion at once.

layout_plan.change: Make the Edit page's top-LEFT dock a TABBED region that swaps Media Pool / Effects / Edit Index, exactly like DaVinci. Today the left column only shows 'Browser' (media, line 1780) or 'Nodes' on the color page (line 1681). Add an 'Effects' tab that surfaces the existing EffectsBrowser.svelte as a Toolbox tree — Transitions, Titles, Generators, Effects — with drag-onto-timeline as the application model, and an 'Edit Index' tab listing every clip in the timeline. All three occupy the same corner and swap via toolbar toggles.
layout_plan.why: The Effects Library is how Resolve users add every transition, title, and filter — drag from the library, drop on the timeline, tweak in the Inspector. Vance has the browser component but never exposes it as the familiar tabbed left dock, so editors can't find effects where they expect them.

layout_plan.change: Convert the single flat Inspector panel (line 2623) into a TABBED, context-sensitive Inspector like DaVinci's: tabs across the top for Video (Transform/Crop/Composite/Retime), Audio (Volume/Pan/EQ), Effects, Transition, and File, auto-selecting the tab that matches the current selection. Keep it docked top-right, full-height.
layout_plan.why: Resolve users expect selecting a clip vs a transition vs a title to reveal different parameter tabs in the same top-right corner. A single undifferentiated Inspector forces them to relearn where each control lives.

layout_plan.change: Add the center COMMAND CLUSTER between the Source and Timeline viewers — Insert, Overwrite, Append, Replace, Snap toggle — as icon buttons. The handlers already exist (insertFromSource at lines 428/436, source mark in/out at 406-420), they're just not surfaced as the familiar between-viewers button strip. Confirm the two viewers read as equal-width 'Source' (left, line 1897) and 'Timeline/Program' (right) with a per-viewer transport row beneath each.
layout_plan.why: The dual-viewer + middle edit-command cluster is the visual signature of Resolve's Edit page; wiring existing actions into that cluster gives editors the exact three-finger workflow (mark in/out on Source → Insert/Overwrite to Timeline) they already know.

layout_plan.change: Add an INTERFACE TOOLBAR strip (~32px) at the top of the Edit page holding the panel toggles (Media Pool / Effects / Edit Index on the left; Inspector / Mixer on the right) as monochrome glyphs that light amber when active, plus a thin EDIT TOOLBAR strip between the timeline viewer and the timeline for tool-mode (Select / Trim / Blade) and toggles (Snapping, Linked Selection, Marker).
layout_plan.why: DaVinci's fixed-dock toggles let editors show/hide panels into known corners rather than hunting menus; the tool/snapping strip above the timeline is where their hands expect the blade and snap controls.

layout_plan.change: Align visual tokens to the Resolve grading-suite look: near-black wells (~#0C0C0E) for the two viewers and the timeline canvas; ~#1E1E1E–#242424 panel bodies; ~#2A2A2E panel headers/toolbars; 1px DARK seams (~#0A0A0A) between panels instead of light borders; keep amber (vance-accent) as the single active accent; add a RED outline for selected timeline clips and an orange track-destination (V1/A1) highlight; 2-3px corner radii everywhere (nothing pill-shaped); 11-13px type; 16px grey→white glyphs. Audit the current vance-border/vance-panel/vance-bg tokens against these values.
layout_plan.why: The dark, flat, low-chroma palette is what signals 'professional NLE' and keeps the UI from biasing the eye against footage; red clip-selection and amber destination are the two color cues Resolve editors read without thinking.

quick_wins: Ship the bottom PAGE BAR first (Media · Edit · Compositor · Color · Audio · Deliver). Replacing the buried Edit/Color toggle + 14-tab dock with a Resolve-style bottom bar is the single change that makes the whole app read as familiar to a DaVinci editor — do it before any panel-level polish.

Purge developer-console leakage app-wide: wrap every raw `String(e)` error (all five panels + onboarding) in a friendly message with the raw text behind a 'Details' toggle; change backend_version() output to just 'Vance 0.1.0'; replace the 'last PTS: 128000' readout with a timecode Position; delete the '(Phase 6.2)' milestone tag. These are the most embarrassing dev tells and the cheapest to fix.

Reskin ExportPanel around outcomes: destination presets named by intent ('Web & social (H.264)', 'High-quality master (ProRes 422 HQ)', 'Editing / archival (DNxHR HQ)'), a 'Quality' slider replacing the 'CRF' field, friendly HDR wording, '(fast)' instead of '(hardware)', 'Save to' instead of 'Out', and a real Movies/Desktop default instead of /tmp. Export is where editors have the most real vocabulary, so this pays off immediately.

Move all install/setup plumbing out of the workflow: relocate AiToolsPanel into Settings → 'Add-ons' as feature cards (name + size + Install + progress + Ready), and strip every pip/Python/PATH/manifest/env-var/Whisper/Demucs string from CaptionsPanel, AiAudioPanel, GeneratePanel and OnboardingWizard. No terminal command or 'Python' should survive anywhere in the UI.

Do the flat label renames that need zero logic changes: dock/page tabs Fusion→Compositor, Magnetic→Magnetic Timeline, Control→Control Surface; MixerConsole Buses→Groups, Gain→Volume, Inserts→Effects, Cmp/Lim→Compressor/Limiter; GeneratePanel steps→Detail, seed→Variation, negative prompt→Things to leave out, W/H→Width/Height. High familiarity payoff, trivial diff.
